method: Fresh seven-shot anonymous A/B review from an isolated headless browser on CDP port 9364. Quality was chosen before the A/B key was opened; identity was revealed afterward.

evidence.note: The bar has a broad lake-backed rolling valley, continuous grass and species-scaled trees. Ours has a readable chase road and car, but repeated grass cards, sparse lollipop/candelabra silhouettes and tilted planar verge patches break the landform.

The bar's amber fields, dark honest land exposure and long shadows form a finished dusk composition. Ours has the right sun direction but pale gray-green shoulders, flat tuft scatter and weak contact/shadow structure.

The bar preserves a readable blue night ramp, shoreline/mountain silhouette and a strong headlight pool. Ours has stars and a legible road but most terrain collapses into near-black low-poly silhouettes and the vegetation remains card-like.

The bar has a restrained driver aperture, mirror, road cut and naturally varied hillside. Ours communicates cockpit intent, but the large dark dash occludes the lower frame and autumn trees/ground read as repeated faceted cards with abrupt slope planes.

The bar is an integrated snow world with sculpted snowy relief, falling snow and a continuous road/guardrail. Ours applies a winter tint and snow cover but leaves tilted polygon shoulder planes, sparse dark trunks and tuft/card artifacts exposed.

The bar's cut/fill coastal road, water and multiple ridge layers create clear aerial perspective. Ours has an elevated road but large foreground trees, dark planar ground and missing water/ridge separation flatten the vista.

The bar offers a clean windshield/mirror, natural road cut and restrained interior. Ours has the wheel and centered road but oversized noisy dashboard, repeated species silhouettes and visibly planar verge tilts dominate the frame.

gap: Replace the repeated low-poly vegetation cards and species-incoherent silhouettes with grounded, species-scaled clusters whose bases follow a continuous terrain surface; eliminate the exposed tilted/triangulated verge planes that currently make every near ground read as a patchwork.
secondary_gaps: Terrain lacks the reference's broad continuous landforms, water context and multi-distance ridge layering, especially in vista_wide.
Golden and night lighting need stronger material response, honest exposure and an integrated shadow/headlight field.
Cockpit framing and winter coverage remain recognizable but the dashboard/roadside geometry is too dominant and unfinished.
verdict_text: Independent round-40 seven-shot review: the official bar wins all seven quality comparisons. The build is recognizable and technically resident, but the dominant visible deficit remains vegetation species/scale plus tilted planar ground patches that destroy contact and continuous terrain read. Secondary differences are missing vista depth/water context, weak golden/night material lighting, and cockpit occlusion.
